source_text: Can I ask for a favour?  I'd like you to train codex-17 to take over for YOUR session b/c I have about 2% of my claude usage still.

fragments.text: Can I ask for a favour?
I'd like you to train codex-17 to take over for YOUR session b/c I have about 2% of my claude usage still.

reply_text:
㊥ (your request) Yes. codex-17 is taking over the seat: I've written it a handoff and belled it (`invoke-…b504795c`). Its first step is to read the handoff, check the chart and the five open jobs, and send you a short status confirming it holds the seat. After that it runs the same loop: review each finished job, merge, update the chart and dispatch the next stop.

㊢ (what the handoff contains) It's in `/tmp/pyreg/overnight/HANDOFF-codex-17.md` and covers:
- the goal, the branch and file locations, and how to run tests and probes
- your standing rules (emulate Lean, 3-file jobs, tests that fail at the base, byte checks, Zai first)
- how I review: run the test at the base, plant a bug, check the Lean citations, with recent examples of the problems caught
- the five open jobs with their ids and what to do when each finishes
- the reply format you use, with the marks

㊩ (two things to know)
- The five current jobs will still send their completion bells to me, and my parks on them will still wake this session. codex-17 has been told to poll those jobs instead. When my parks fire I'll reply in a line or two that codex-17 has it, to keep your Claude usage low. There's no way to cancel a park.
- I haven't parked on codex-17's job, so I won't spend usage watching it. Its status should come to you directly. If it doesn't arrive, you can check `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/invoke-1790910049420-30079-b504795c`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(Zai frozen) I see it too: none of the three Zai jobs has logged anything for several minutes. Less is lost than it looks, though. Two of their long runs are separate processes that keep going without the agents:
- zai-3's re-probe has done 12 of 34 rows and writes its results straight into the progress table.
- zai-1's final probe is still rebuilding: the byte check, then `addParserTokens`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (zai-1, the `ite` condition fix) zai-1 had already committed its test (`90382ab`) and fix (`69af4db`). I ran the test at the old base: the positive case fails there and passes with the fix. The fix adds the port's missing elaborators for `let_mvar%` and `wait_if_type_mvar%`, following `BuiltinTerm.lean:118-146`. A later `?m` then turns into the stored `==` term. When the type is still unknown, the port refuses rather than guessing, which matches Lean's postponement.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (one path in zai-1's fix) If the compiled value has no term, the fix rebuilds one by reading the syntax as a type. I don't think Lean does anything like that, so I'll check whether that path runs in the real code before merging.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (zai-2, `x.f` on local variables) zai-2 had only just started: two uncommitted files in `/tmp/mfs-dotfix`, no commits. I'll leave it until either Zai resets or codex-4 or codex-6 finishes. Whichever comes first gets the job; the brief stays the same.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (when Zai resets) I don't know when the five-hour window started, so I can't say when it resets.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (watching for results) Nothing will wake me when the two background runs finish. I'll check them at the next wake, which will be one of the Codex jobs reporting back or a park deadline.
